wording: Figures are for tax year 2026. This Guide covers the German side only: the exit tax on company shares under § 6 of the Foreign Tax Act (Außensteuergesetz, AStG) and the extended limited tax liability under § 2 AStG that can follow a move to a low-tax country. It reads the current consolidated text on gesetze-im-internet.de, which applies to income tax from the 2022 assessment year onwards (§ 21(1) AStG). Departures before 1 January 2022 follow the old wording of § 6 (§ 21(3) AStG) and are out of scope. This is a working paper for review, not a filed return.

The test is about the company's capital, not about the company's country, so shares in a German GmbH and in a foreign company both count. See [§ 17 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__17.html).

wording: 2. Test the person. § 6 applies only to a natural person who was fully taxable in Germany (unbeschränkt steuerpflichtig under § 1(1) EStG) for at least seven years in total within the twelve years before the triggering event. For shares received free of charge (gift or inheritance), the periods of the giver count too, and overlapping periods count once. See [§ 6(2) AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__6.html).

wording: 3. Identify the trigger and its date. There are three triggers in § 6(1) AStG: the end of full tax liability because the person gives up the German residence or habitual abode (taxed at the moment liability ends); a free transfer of the shares to a person who is not fully taxable in Germany (taxed at the moment of transfer); and any other exclusion or restriction of Germany's right to tax the gain on the shares (taxed immediately before that happens). See [§ 6(1) AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__6.html).

wording: 4. Compute the deemed gain. The trigger counts as a sale of the shares at their fair market value (gemeiner Wert). The gain is that value less sale costs less acquisition cost (§ 17(2) EStG), and it is business income (§ 17(1) EStG). Apply the partial-income method: the exempt share in the § 3 table below (§ 3 no. 40 letter c EStG); sale costs and the acquisition cost just used to compute the gain are themselves deductible only at the share in the § 3c table below, because § 3c(2) EStG's second half-sentence extends the same limit to acquisition cost taken into account in determining income. Then apply the § 17(3) allowance, which is scaled to the share sold and shrinks as the gain grows. See [§ 17 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__17.html), [§ 3 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__3.html) and [§ 3c EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__3c.html).

wording: **Who.** Only natural persons. The seven-year test counts years of full tax liability under § 1(1) EStG, in total, not in a row. Where the shares were received free of charge, the full tax liability of the giver (and of each earlier giver in a chain of free transfers) is added, and years in which both were fully taxable count only once. A person whose earlier exit tax lapsed because they came back is treated as covered without the seven-year test, and so is their direct or indirect successor (§ 6(2) sentence 4 AStG).

wording: **Which shares.** Shares within § 17(1) sentence 1 EStG. § 17(1) sentence 3 defines them: shares (Aktien), GmbH shares, profit participation rights (Genussscheine) and similar participations, rights to acquire such shares, and shares in a company that opted to be taxed as a corporation under § 1a KStG. Shares in a cooperative also count (§ 17(7) EStG). § 6(1) AStG applies subject to the rules of the Income Tax Act, the Corporation Tax Act and the Reorganisation Tax Act, so shares held as business assets need a separate check (see "When to refuse or refer").

wording: The deemed sale is a sale under § 17(1) EStG, and § 17(1) sentence 1 makes that gain income from business (Einkünfte aus Gewerbebetrieb). The gain is the amount by which the sale price, after sale costs, exceeds the acquisition cost (§ 17(2) sentence 1 EStG); for § 6 AStG the sale price is the fair market value. Acquisition cost includes incidental costs and later costs such as open or hidden capital contributions (§ 17(2a) EStG). Under § 3c(2) EStG, this acquisition cost is itself deductible only at the share in the § 3c table below, not in full: its second half-sentence reaches "die Anschaffungs- oder Herstellungskosten ... mindernd zu berücksichtigen sind", not only sale costs.
